newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot natgas little changed ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas little changed ahead of weekend.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were little changed in a quiet Friday session as additional supply returned to the market and storage injections continued, traders said.
Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was quoted at C$1.49-1.51 per gigajoule early and about C$1.53-1.54 late, indicating a decrease of about one cent from Thursday.
"People are expecting more receipts to come back," one Calgary-based trader said, noting AECO prices for delivery on Saturday and Sunday were quoted at a slight discount to next-day at C$1.52-1.53.
July AECO was talked at C$1.47-1.49 per GJ, while one-year AECO was quoted at C$1.70.
Canadian Gas Association (CGA) said earlier today that gas stocks in the West were at 86.07 bcf, or 33.2 percent full, versus 41.2 percent a year ago.
At Sumas, Wash., prices held in the mid-to-high teens per million British thermal units (mmBtu) in light trade.
According to Weather Services Corp, temperature highs throughout Washington were forecast to reach the high-60s to low-70s F over the weekend, creating very little demand in the region.
In the East, prices at Niagara gained about three cents to the low-to-mid $2.30s per mmBtu in response to the early uptick on NYMEX.
July Henry Hub gas futures rose this morning to a high of $2.214, up 3.7 cents.

CGA also reported that eastern stocks were at 34.84 bcf, or 15 percent full, versus 15.6 percent a year ago and 12.1 percent a week ago. Overall Canadian stocks were at 120.91 bcf, or 24.6 percent full, compared with 29.6 percent in 1996.
